rowDiagnosis.currentBody:
Typical consideration: Lobby zoning, meeting pre-function, and social spaces may need to reflect upscale positioning—furniture families, art, and digital guest messaging are commonly controlled.
Owner planning consideration: Ceiling heights, storefront, and co-tenancy rules affect entitlement; upscale refresh can exceed select-service conversion cost.
Typical status: Confirm with brand
Notes to confirm: Applies to: New build and conversion

rowDiagnosis.title: QA, Inspection & Ongoing Compliance
rowDiagnosis.currentBody:
Typical consideration: Pre-opening inspection, annual QA, and mystery-guest programs may apply with scored remediation and reinspection fees.
Owner planning consideration: Reserve management time and capital for action plans; understand fee exposure for repeat failures.
Typical status: Confirm with brand
Notes to confirm: Applies to: Opening and stabilized operations

rowDiagnosis.title: Sustainability, Accessibility & Life Safety
rowDiagnosis.currentBody:
Typical consideration: Brand sustainability playbooks and accessibility targets may exceed local code; life safety and brand fire-life-safety reviews are typically non-negotiable.
Owner planning consideration: Early coordination on EV charging, water programs, and accessible room dispersion; do not assume code compliance alone satisfies brand.
Typical status: Confirm with brand
Notes to confirm: Applies to: New build and renovation

rowDiagnosis.title: Design Review, Plans & Submittals
rowDiagnosis.currentBody:
Typical consideration: Architectural, interior, and MEP submittals usually pass through brand design review with milestone gates before construction.
Owner planning consideration: Budget design review fees, consultant rework cycles, and schedule float for resubmittals.
Typical status: Confirm with brand
Notes to confirm: Applies to: New build and material renovation Abbreviated review may be available for recent sister-flag renovations—document in writing.

rowDiagnosis.currentBody:
Typical consideration: Restaurant, bar, or enhanced market concepts may be required or optional by prototype; kitchen exhaust, hood, and liquor scope vary by market.
Owner planning consideration: Operator model (self-op vs. lease), daypart staffing, and brand F&B audits should be modeled before LOI.
Typical status: Confirm with brand
Notes to confirm: Applies to: Properties with in-scope F&B Contract F&B operators still typically require brand concept approval.

rowDiagnosis.title: Guestroom, Bath & Sleep Experience
rowDiagnosis.currentBody:
Typical consideration: Room modules, casegoods, lighting, and bath specifications are often tied to approved prototypes; mattress and linen programs are usually mandated.
Owner planning consideration: Lead times for casegoods and bath packages drive opening dates; partial conversions may require room-type-by-room PIP schedules.
Typical status: Confirm with brand
Notes to confirm: Applies to: All guest-facing projects Soft conversions may defer non-visible items only with brand approval.

rowDiagnosis.title: Technology, CRS & Loyalty Programs
rowDiagnosis.currentBody:
Typical consideration: PMS, CRS, Wi-Fi, digital key, and guest apps are typically prescribed; Choice portfolio connectivity and loyalty enrollment are usually mandatory at cutover.
Owner planning consideration: Plan parallel runs, data migration, and channel-manager mapping to avoid double bookings and rate parity issues.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Applies to: All operating hotels Legacy systems on conversion are often allowed for a limited transition period only.

Typical status: Confirm with brand
Notes to confirm: Applies to: Hotels with meeting inventory

Owner planning consideration: Map which elements are mandatory at opening vs. within a post-opening compliance window; budget for brand-approved vendors where specified.
Typical status: Confirm with brand
Notes to confirm: Applies to: New build, conversion, and reflag Sister-flag conversions may reuse certain FF&E or signage with written waivers.

rowDiagnosis.title: PIP, Conversion & Sister-Flag Transitions
rowDiagnosis.currentBody:
Typical consideration: PIP line items are often itemized by FF&E, soft goods, signage, and technology; scope may be lighter when retaining compatible assets from the same parent.
Owner planning consideration: Tie PIP funding to incentive package; separate mandatory opening items from 12–24 month deferrals in LOI discussions.
Typical status: May Apply
Notes to confirm: Applies to: Conversion and reflag Prior PIP completion within 24–36 months may reduce scope—confirm eligibility.
